report:
Codex PASS lacked valid task or source evidence for every premise. PASS concerns the entire restricted scalar-Hopf A–G theorem, under the exact BMP and gauge theorems granted by the task. The current manuscript and the complete cold reconstruction establish its essential claims. Previous verdicts, reading records and symbolic checks supply no mathematical premises.

A: The radial action is free and properly discontinuous; polar coordinates give the compact connected smooth quotient S⁵×S¹. The charts z₀=eʷ identify the fibers with E and establish the elliptic submersion. The complementary ranks of α and β give h>0, and differentiation gives dh=−ds∧α≠0. I checked the [Xia–Zhang construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.21053v1), including its heat estimates, completed square, startup, small-time, large-time and cutoff regimes, integrable negative deficit, and final smooth correction. The correction preserves strict positivity and divergent fiber energy on a fixed base ball. These are actual smooth bounded potentials, so they establish v₊(h)=∞.

B: Closure works for arbitrary smooth, including nonclosed, backgrounds. For smooth inputs and Fδ=δ log Σ exp(wᵢ/δ), with pᵢ=exp(wᵢ/δ)/Σ exp(wⱼ/δ), the exact identity is θ+D Fδ=Σ pᵢ(θ+D wᵢ)+δ⁻¹Σ pᵢ d(wᵢ−Fδ)∧dᶜ(wᵢ−Fδ). The last term is positive. Convolution approximates the common smooth background uniformly, so passage to the limit retains the exact Hessian bound. Countable selection and finite maxima, including one fixed competitor, produce a noncollapsed canonical envelope.

On every local modification, the pulled increasing sequence has a common local quasi-psh bound, a fixed integrable lower competitor and local L¹ convergence. Its canonical limit agrees with the pullback envelope off the exceptional locus, hence everywhere. Lelong semicontinuity preserves each divisorial lower bound; domination of the fixed competitor supplies the reverse bound. The order asymptotics and the uniform-margin [valuative integrability criterion](https://sebastien.boucksom.perso.math.cnrs.fr/notes/L2.pdf) then retain all ideals at every real weight. This includes every local exceptional divisor. Normalization, idempotence and the nested-background identity follow from the resulting equality of competitor classes. Taking a maximum with the admissible input also identifies the equality envelope with the corresponding ideal-inclusion envelope.

The submersion assertion covers all holomorphic germs. [Demailly’s tensor-product theorem](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/source_files/pdf/trieste.pdf), with base weight tu/2 and fiber weight zero, gives the exact ideal pullback. The cold Taylor/Parseval proof independently covers arbitrary germs: all Taylor coefficients belong to the coherent base ideal, and the Noetherian local Krull intersection theorem closes the passage from finite truncations. Fubini on lifted germs reflects ideal equality downstairs.

The entire ambient competitor family is invariant under E, so its canonical envelope is invariant and descends. Local product coordinates give bh+D M=π*(bκ+D w)+bβ. Testing positivity with smooth horizontal lifts annihilating β and positive fiber densities proves base positivity distributionally. Local integrability and uniqueness of canonical representatives identify M=π*w everywhere, including poles. Every base competitor lifts, proving both inequalities in the fiber-envelope identity. No restriction to basic ambient competitors or ambient mass monotonicity is used.

G: Scalar invariance supplies genuine descents Γτ^(εh)=π*φτ^ε. The fiber identity proves that these are normalized base ideal models. Scalar compatibility establishes equality of all positive-slice ideals at each fixed τ. For any positive smooth ξ, choose δκ≤ξ and define Ψτ^ξ=P_(κ+ξ)[φτ^δ]_I. The input is admissible, and equality of scalar ideal classes makes this definition independent of δ. It reproduces the scalar slices and establishes compatibility for every ξ, including nonclosed ξ.

Decrease follows by taking the maximum of a later competitor and the earlier scalar input. For concavity, the intermediate input has divisorial orders no greater than the corresponding convex combination of endpoint orders. Taking the maximum of that convex combination of competitors and the intermediate input restores exactly every target order. Complete suprema and canonical regularization establish the pointwise inequalities throughout the interval, including poles; zero coefficients at endpoints are omitted. Constancy for τ≤a follows from the inputs. The original genuine ambient limit descends to ψτ, and its model property gives the base model property. For every auxiliary base metric k, bounds lκ≤k≤rκ give φτ^(l/j)≤Ψτ^(k/j)≤φτ^(r/j). This proves the genuine metric-independent decreasing limit, with canonical values at poles. Equality of positive-slice and limiting ideals was not assumed.

C: Bounded κ-psh potentials have mass one, so the closed projective base has BMP. All full-system hypotheses required by the task-granted recovery theorem have now been established. Positive initial lower ordinary-type volume therefore gives base recovery at every finite τ<c. The fiber identity gives scalar ambient recovery. For arbitrary η>0, choose εh≤η; original compatibility and the nested-background identity then give Γτ^η=P_(h+η)[Γτ]_I. No finite upper-volume deficit on the Hopf manifold enters this argument.

D: Uniform L¹ bounds for the normalized hyperplane logarithms make S=Σqⱼℓⱼ noncollapsed. Both current source and cold notes correctly use ψ₀=S−sup S. The inputs satisfy κ+D uτ≥(1−λmax)κ and h+Dπ*uτ≥(1−λmax)h. Consequently all proposed envelopes are nonempty. The closure and maximum arguments establish normalization, compatibility, whole-interval decrease and concavity. Their decreasing limits retain the input orders by semicontinuity and domination, and are exactly the unperturbed ideal envelopes; scalar squeezing proves independence of every perturbing metric.

In coefficient normalization, every local divisor F has order λ(τ)Σqⱼ ord_F(Hⱼ), with the corresponding composite pullbacks upstairs. Positive-current summation and the divisorial restriction formula justify this identity even at accumulation points and on exceptional divisors. No additional coefficient is silently discarded. Infinitely many positive prime-divisor orders exclude an analytic singularity type, including an ideal-equivalent analytic type.

Positive [non-pluripolar multilinearity](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674) gives initial input mass at least (1−λ₀)². [Witt Nyström’s theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01950v1) transfers this bound to the base model without an analytic-singularity or small-unbounded-locus hypothesis. Applying the theorem in both ordinary-order directions proves equal mass for every ordinarily equivalent genuine competitor. Thus the asserted lower ordinary-type volume, rather than a raw ambient mass, is positive. Together with A, this is a nonvacuous recovery example with genuinely unbounded ambient upper mass.

E: At the exact pulled closed base background, every potential descends on the isomorphism locus. Local psh extension and canonical uniqueness establish the descent everywhere, including exceptional poles. This gives the complete correspondence of potentials, normalization and ordinary types. Actual non-pluripolar measures agree off the exceptional sets and charge neither those sets nor their images; taking the infimum over all corresponding competitors preserves the lower volume exactly. [Darvas–Xia Lemma 3.1](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/542539/file/542539_Fulltext.pdf) has the required compact Kähler, closed big-background hypotheses. Its inclusion-envelope convention agrees here with the task’s equality envelope by the separately proved maximum and closure argument. The modification formula includes the relative canonical/Jacobian correction. Arbitrary ambient modifications preserve the pulled local divisorial constraints; no nonclosed numerical-volume invariance or recovery for new modified perturbation systems follows or is claimed.

F: Gauge transport retains π, E, κ, α, β and the original geometric metric h while replacing the background by h+D f. The strict potential −f verifies bigness. The transported normalized slices are the prescribed zero-obstacle ideal envelopes of Γτ^η−f; simply subtracting f is not the normalization operation. The task-granted gauge theorem preserves the already established recovery. Newly normalized gauged slices need not be basic. The classical positive-initial-ambient-lower-volume BMP branch remains distinct from the transverse branch. The cited valuative, envelope, modification, mass-monotonicity and Hopf-construction results constitute substantial literature overlap; this audit makes no priority certification.

Convention and wording checks: The new four-line clarification is correct. The manuscript uses ν(log|z|)=1, so ν(log|f|²)=2 ord(f), and the coefficient of [F] in Dφ is ν_F(φ)/2. The cold notes use that coefficient convention directly. With I(tu)=J(tu/2), their displayed bounds agree. The obsolete applications note’s instruction to scale Xia–Zhang’s potentials is wrong and explicitly superseded: keep each potential unchanged while dividing the operator and background forms by 2π; masses scale by (2π)⁻³. Increasing envelopes converge canonically through L¹ convergence and usc regularization, not necessarily as the raw pointwise supremum at every pole. These clarifications require no substantial repair of the current argument. Where legacy PDF endpoints timed out, supplied complete excerpts were checked against matching primary indexed passages or published mirrors.

The unrestricted original P19 is not completed. A general replacement invariant and uniform estimates beyond BMP, together with specialization of a general new extension to the BMP theorem, remain open. Retaining the classical BMP branch separately does not discharge those original obligations.

For a local psh function φ, J(φ) defined by |f|²exp(−2φ), every prime divisor F over a smooth chart and every positive integer k satisfy ν_F(φ)−A(F)/k≤ord_F J(kφ)/k≤ν_F(φ), where ν(log|z|)=1 and A(F) is the log discrepancy.

For a psh weight φ near x on a smooth complex manifold and a nonzero holomorphic germ f, f∈J(φ)_x if and only if there exists ε>0 such that ord_F(f)≥(1+ε)ν_F(φ)−A(F) for every prime divisor F over a sufficiently small neighborhood whose center contains x; J uses exp(−2φ) and ν(log|z|)=1.

passages.statement: For every local psh weight φ, the ideal I(φ) defined using |f|²exp(−φ) satisfies I(φ)=∪_{ε>0}I((1+ε)φ).

For local psh functions converging in L¹_loc, the limiting pointwise Lelong number is at least the limsup of their Lelong numbers. Pointwise Lelong numbers satisfy ν(max(u,v))=min(ν(u),ν(v)) and ν(u+v)=ν(u)+ν(v).

passages.statement: For a psh weight φ, its multiplier ideal J(φ), defined using exp(−2φ), is coherent; on a bounded Stein open set it is generated by any Hilbert basis of the weighted holomorphic L² space.

For complex manifolds X₁,X₂, psh weights φ₁,φ₂ and projections p_i:X₁×X₂→X_i, the multiplier ideals defined using exp(−2φ) satisfy J(p₁*φ₁+p₂*φ₂)=p₁*J(φ₁)·p₂*J(φ₂) as ideal sheaves, including all holomorphic germs.
For a modification μ:Y→X of smooth complex manifolds and a psh weight φ on X, μ_*(O(K_Y/X)⊗J(φ∘μ))=J(φ), where J uses exp(−2φ).

On a compact Kähler manifold with a smooth closed real (1,1) background θ, arbitrary genuine θ-psh φ,ψ satisfying φ≥ψ+C obey ∫MA_θ(φ)≥∫MA_θ(ψ), without an analytic-singularity or small-unbounded-locus hypothesis.

passages.statement: Non-pluripolar products of closed positive (1,1) currents on compact Kähler manifolds are well-defined and finite, positive, symmetric, multilinear, local in the plurifine topology and give no mass to pluripolar sets; for a compact Kähler modification μ, their pushforward from the pulled currents equals the product downstairs.

Non-pluripolar products of closed positive (1,1) currents on compact Kähler manifolds are well-defined and finite, positive, symmetric, multilinear, local in the plurifine topology and give no mass to pluripolar sets; for a compact Kähler modification μ, their pushforward from the pulled currents equals the product downstairs.
For a Kähler form κ on a compact complex manifold and every bounded κ-psh u, the Bedford–Taylor mass ∫(κ+dd^c u)^n equals ∫κ^n.
passages.quote: computed in cohomology, and hence is independent of k

passages.statement: For a smooth modification μ:Y→X between compact Kähler manifolds, a smooth closed big background θ and u∈PSH(X,θ), Darvas–Xia Lemma 3.1 gives μ*P_θ[u]_I=P_(μ*θ)[μ*u]_I; its source envelope uses competitors v≤0 with I(tv)⊆I(tu) for every t>0, I(tu) uses exp(−tu), and dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π).

For a closed positive (1,1) current T and a prime divisor F, the restriction of its coefficient measures to F satisfies 1_F T=ν(T,F)[F]; ν(T,F) is the infimum of the pointwise Lelong numbers along F and equals their value outside a countable union of proper analytic subsets.
If R is a Noetherian local ring, I is a proper ideal and M is a finite R-module, then ∩_{n≥0}I^nM=0.
The ring of convergent complex power-series germs C{z₁,…,z_n} is Noetherian.

A locally uniformly upper-bounded family of psh functions has a countable subfamily with the same usc supremum; that supremum is psh and agrees almost everywhere with the raw supremum unless it is identically minus infinity.
passages.quote: is plurisubharmonic and is equal to u almost everywhere

passages.statement: A locally integrable distribution with positive distributional complex Hessian has a unique genuine psh representative. The psh cone is closed under local L¹ convergence; locally L¹-bounded families are relatively compact in local L¹. A decreasing noncollapsed sequence of psh functions has its genuine pointwise psh limit.
A psh function on the complement of a closed pluripolar subset extends uniquely as a psh function across that subset if it is locally bounded above near it.

For psh germs u,v at 0∈C^n, equality of their pointwise Lelong numbers at every point over 0 on every proper smooth modification is equivalent to J_+(tu)=J_+(tv) for every t>0, where J uses exp(−2φ) and J_+(φ) is the stationary value of J((1+ε)φ) as ε decreases to zero.

For a full compatible envelope system in a BMP background, positivity of the initial limiting lower ordinary-type volume implies recovery at every finite slice; the task grants this theorem for the full closed base system.
passages.quote: Under BMP, positivity of the initial limiting lower volume suffices: a finite upper-volume deficit gives stretches with uniformly controlled divisorial errors, and concavity propagates positivity to each finite slice.

passages.statement: Smooth gauge transport θ′=θ+dd^c f with normalized transported ideal envelopes P_(θ′)[Γ−f]_I preserves recovery.
passages.quote: Smooth gauge transport by theta prime=theta+dd^c f and Gamma prime=P_(theta prime)[Gamma-f]_I preserves recovery.
